title: Parent-level scoring; a recipe sweep (R1-R3) and a second base model (G1) on E2's data
question: With the annotators' parent-or-sub-technique habit taken out of the score, does a longer or larger training recipe, or a different 4B base model, name the right technique family more often than E2 on real-report statements?
motivation: Owner's decision (2026-10-15) after four data additions and two loss changes moved nothing beyond noise: (1) score at parent level, since 111 of E2's 131 right-family exact misses on CTI-HAL are granularity, not a wrong sibling; (2) vary the recipe, which has had one setting (2 epochs, LoRA r 16, LoRA lr 1e-4, head lr 1e-3) and whose last dev curve was still rising; (3) try a second base, since Cribl's adapter added nothing over a fresh LoRA (B1 vs B2 +0.003).
harness: relabel_parents.py (cases_<split>_parents.jsonl), parent_rescore.py (parent-level, family and exact with paired CIs), family_head.py (--base, --lora-r, --selection parent; parent_level in every exact block), prepare_cti_rationale.py (validation reports as a selection set), runpod/remote_sweep.sh

metric.parent_level: the answered technique's parent is among the gold ids' parents (common.hits parent-aware on technique_pick); equals exact on the parent-relabelled files
metric.informed_by_part_a: E2 on CTI-HAL: family top-1 0.642, parent level 0.639, exact 0.514; public test 0.633 / 0.636 / 0.561; AnnoCTR test 0.717 / 0.714 / 0.451; CTI-Rationale test 0.517 / 0.517 / 0.421 (parent_rescore_*.json, 2026-10-15, before any new run)

data.training: E2's five files unchanged: cases_train_clean, cases_annoctr_train_clean, cases_attack_train_clean, cases_advisories_train, cases_atomic_train (26,353 rows); no CTI-Rationale rows
data.selection: cases_dev (659), cases_annoctr_dev (336) and cases_cti_rationale_validation (221 paragraphs of the dataset's 15 validation reports, built with the same leakage guards, 10 paragraphs overlapping training text dropped); selection score = mean over the three of parent level (the family answer where a run has no technique head); ties: the earlier checkpoint
data.confirmation: public test (1,391), clean AnnoCTR test (738), CTI-Rationale test (209) on the pod; CTI-HAL (968) on the laptop

runs.R1: E2's recipe for 3 epochs (init cribl, LoRA r 16, LoRA lr 1e-4, head lr 1e-3)
runs.R3: R1 with a fresh LoRA of rank 64 (alpha 128); Cribl's r-16 adapter cannot change rank, so this run also changes the init (B2 vs B1 showed fresh = cribl within +0.003; the confound is noted)
runs.G1: google/gemma-4-E4B@411aa17b (Apache 2.0; 4.5B effective parameters) with a fresh LoRA r 16 on the attention projections, E2's recipe (2 epochs, LoRA lr 1e-4, head lr 1e-3), the family prompt in Gemma's turn format with the same body; the family and technique heads start from the base's own ATT&CK-text states as always
runs.common: seed 7, 16 examples per step, a checkpoint every half epoch (every quarter for E2), 4-bit NF4 base, RunPod secure RTX 4090 (R1-R3 ~105 min at $0.89/h, G1 ~125 min)

success.headline_recipe: CTI-HAL parent level, the sweep run with the best selection score minus E2, paired 95% CI (1000 samples, seed 7) lower bound above 0
success.headline_base: CTI-HAL parent level, G1 minus E2, CI lower bound above 0
secondary: public test parent level, same run minus E2 (tram / expert / derived_procedures reported separately)
AnnoCTR test family top-1, same run minus E2
CTI-Rationale test parent level, same run minus E2
non-inferiority on public test family top-1: CI lower bound above -0.02
success.reported: every checkpoint's three dev scores; family top-1 and strict exact on every set; the other two sweep runs on every set; rare-family subset (gold family with fewer than 100 training rows); calibration (ECE); peak GPU memory and time per example; G1's Gemma module match count and quantised-module list from the laptop pilot

limitation: three recipe runs pick one setting each on dev, so the best of three carries a small selection optimism (about half a point); G1 changes the base and the LoRA init at once, by design; CTI-HAL's two annotators agree about 65-70% of the time, so gains near the ceiling may not show
stop_rules: more than 1% of a split's cases end in error
G1: the LoRA matches no module, or a quantised module list that includes the embeddings
confirmation_runs: each run's selected checkpoint once on the public test, AnnoCTR test and CTI-Rationale test (pod) and CTI-HAL (laptop); nothing is chosen, refit or rerun because of a confirmation result; a combined run (best recipe on the best base) is a follow-up with its own registration
informed_by: Part A (parent-level rescoring of E1/E2/E3/F2/M1/M2, above) and the laptop pilots (mechanics only: rank 64 fresh LoRA on 96 rows; Gemma 4 E4B loads, trains 96 rows, saves and reloads). No sweep or Gemma model exists.
